newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan, U.N. council condemn killing of Israeli girls.
newsitem.headline: Annan, U.N. council condemn killing of Israeli girls.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan and the Security Council condemned the killing on Thursday of seven Israeli schoolgirls by a Jordanian soldier on the border between the two countries.
A spokesman for Annan said in a statement the U.N. chief "deplores this act of violence and extends condolences to the families of the victims and the government and people of Israel."

"Today's tragic incident highlights the need to renew confidence in the peace process whose objective is the achievement of a comprehensive, just and lasting settlement in the Middle East," the statement added.

Council President Zbigniew Wlosowicz of Poland told reporters that council members "learned with great sorrow and concern of the tragic attack on Israeli children earlier today near the Jordan river."
"Such terrible attacks on innocent people are despicable and deserve the condemnation of all," he said, adding that council members extended condolences to the families of the victims.

The incident occurred at a time when the peace process is at a low ebb as a result of a number of recent developments, including a widely-criticised Israeli decision to build new Jewish housing in Arab East Jerusalem.

The General Assembly was expected to adopt a resolution by a large majority later in the day calling on Israel to rescind its decision to build 6,500 homes for Jews on a tree-lined hill between East Jerusalem and Bethlehem called Har Homa by Israel and Jabal Abu Ghneim by the Palestinians.
